observations: Moore vs Mealy: the 6-mark 'Distinguish between Moore machine and Mealy machine' question appears in 4 of 6 papers (Summer 2023, Winter 2023, Summer 2024, Winter 2024); Winter 2022 asked a Moore-to-Mealy conversion and Moore machine MCQs appear in Winter 2024 and Summer 2025, so every paper carries Moore/Mealy content.

Chomsky classification/hierarchy: a descriptive question appears in all 6 papers but under different wordings. 'Explain Chomsky classification of grammar' repeats 3 times (Summer 2023, Winter 2023, Winter 2024); 'Explain in brief Chomsky hierarchy with suitable examples' repeats twice (Winter 2022, Summer 2025); Summer 2024 asked it as 'Type 0 / 1 / 2 / 3 grammar' and is kept as a separate question.

Grammar simplification (null, unit or useless-symbol elimination) appears in all 6 papers, but only the Winter 2022 and Summer 2025 null-production question is an exact repeat; the other papers use different grammars.

Summer 2025 overlaps heavily with earlier papers: 12 of its 13 descriptive questions repeat an earlier question verbatim (11 from Winter 2022 and 1 from Winter 2023); only 'What is FA? Explain with examples...' (Q2B) is new.
Objective questions (1 mark each) appear only in Winter 2024 and Summer 2025; 10 of the 12 MCQs in each paper are the same question, with only options reordered or slightly reworded.

Turing-machine design questions (palindromes, equal a's and b's, strings ending with 00, second letter b, erasing symbols) appear in every paper; the palindrome TM, the equal a's/b's TM (Winter 2022 wording) and the Halting Problem each repeat in Winter 2022 and Summer 2025.

PDA components appears in 3 papers (Summer 2023, Summer 2024, Winter 2024) and Deterministic vs Non-deterministic PDA in 2 (Summer 2023, Winter 2023); CFG-to-PDA conversion appears in 3 papers (Winter 2022, Summer 2024, Summer 2025) with two different grammars.

Derivation trees / leftmost-rightmost derivations appear in 4 papers (Winter 2022, Winter 2023, Winter 2024, Summer 2025); CNF conversion in 4 papers (Winter 2022, Summer 2023, Winter 2023, Summer 2025).

Applications of regular expressions appear in 3 papers (Summer 2023, Summer 2024, Winter 2024); only the Summer 2023 and Summer 2024 wordings are identical, the Winter 2024 version adds three regular-expression-writing tasks.

Unit 5 in the supplied papers is limited to Chomsky hierarchy and the Halting Problem (plus one Universal Turing Machine sub-part); most Unit 5 syllabus topics (decidability, PCP, LBA, context-sensitive languages, properties of recursive/RE languages) were not found, and absence from these papers does not mean they are unimportant.

Several Unit 1 and Unit 2 syllabus topics (DFA minimization, epsilon elimination, DFA-to-RE conversion, pumping lemma) and Unit 3 topics (pumping lemma for CFLs, properties of CFLs) were not found in the supplied papers.

notes: Six papers were supplied, all for BTCOC502 Theory of Computation: Winter 2022 (paper dated 31-01-2023), Summer 2023 (supplementary), Winter 2023 (dated 03/01/2024), Summer 2024 (supplementary), Winter 2024 (dated 08/02/2025) and Summer 2025 (rescheduled supplementary). subject_code is taken from these papers.

exam_year is the year printed in each paper's title, not the actual date of the sitting. years_asked uses session-plus-year labels (for example 'Winter 2024') because two papers fall in 2024 and two in 2023.

Every objective question, every A/B/C part and every 'solve any two' choice is stored as its own record (110 appearances). MCQs have question_number 1 and the item number as subquestion_number; marks are as printed (1 for MCQs, 6 for descriptive parts).

Original wording is preserved. Where text extraction dropped symbols, only the symbol was restored: arrows (→) in grammar productions, ^ and _ for superscripts and subscripts, and Σ. Typos in the printed paper (for example 'turning machine') are kept.
Level/CO annotations printed beside each question are not stored because the required schema has no field for them.

Repetition groups require substantially identical wording and requirements. Not grouped: Summer 2024 Q3B (Type 0–3 grammars) with the Chomsky classification group; Summer 2024 Q5C (TM for equal a's and b's) with the Winter 2022/Summer 2025 TM question, because that wording is unclear; Winter 2024 Q2A (applications plus three RE-writing tasks) with the applications-only questions; Winter 2023 Q5B (halt state plus Church–Turing thesis) with Summer 2023 Q5C; Winter 2024 MCQ 11 with Summer 2025 MCQ 10; questions that use different grammars or automata (NFA to DFA, CNF, null and grammar reduction, CFG to PDA).

The PDA components group tolerates small wording additions ('What is PDA?' in Summer 2024, 'with neat diagram' in Summer 2023); the PDA n_a = n_b group tolerates the '(ab)*' vs '(a,b)*' printing difference.
Topic priority is based on the number of distinct papers a topic appears in: high for 4 or more, medium for 2 or 3, low for 1. total_appearances counts every record, so MCQs count as appearances.

No question was classified as out_of_syllabus; questions whose topic is not named in the supplied syllabus are marked verification_needed or partially_aligned and listed in mapping_needs_verification.
Analysis covers only the six supplied papers. Syllabus topics not found are listed in syllabus_coverage and are not marked unimportant.
